headers.before: The King of the East receives him politely, which is its own kind of answer.
headers.label: The Eastern Court
headers.why: Munhee packing in Surabol → Yamato audience; the sea crossing happens between two sentences

headers.before: He starts counting who would come with him, and the first door he knocks on is Alchun’s.
headers.label: Alchun’s Door
headers.why: palace gate with Seungman → Alchun's house; same scene label still says Princess Seungman

headers.before: That night Bidam takes the old black headband out of the chest
headers.label: That Night
headers.why: queen's chamber in uproar → Bidam alone at home, hours later

headers.before: On Earth, the people sing a song to call for a new king.
headers.label: Mount Guji
headers.why: sky-and-ridge love scene → villagers on earth singing the turtle song

headers.before: Queen Heo, an Indian princess, becomes the first queen of Golden Gaya.
headers.label: The Red Sail
headers.why: Gaya league exposition → Heo's arrival; new lead character, years later

headers.before: Two nights in a tent by the water before anyone may say marriage.
headers.label: The Tent by the Water
headers.why: hill rite → tent on the shore, two nights

headers.before: Bidam and Yumjong raise men at the Fortress of Radiance.
headers.label: The Fortress of Radiance
headers.why: queen's sickbed → rebel rampart, inside Day 1

headers.before: Before noon Alchun is summoned twice — once by the Sword of Silla
headers.label: Between the Camps
headers.why: rampart → Alchun shuttling between the two camps

headers.before: This is the first time the cavern goddesses meet Bupmin.
headers.label: The Steam Cavern
headers.why: Moon Palace (Chunchu hands over the jar) → the goddesses' cavern

headers.before: If Bidam wins, the Secretariat becomes a quaint hobby.
headers.label: Chunchu’s Rooms
headers.why: pavilion splash → Chunchu talking to Munhee at home; Munhee appears with no cue

headers.before: Thirty years earlier, the last lord of Geumgwan had already handed his kingdom over
headers.label: The Surrender
headers.why: 562 Daegaya conquest → jump back thirty years to Geumgwan's surrender hall

headers.before: The rebel shout shakes the ground. Inside the Moon Palace Queen Sunduk goes pale.
headers.label: The Moon Palace
headers.why: Bidam at the rebel lines → inside the palace with the queen and Yushin

headers.before: The kite buys one night. A sky can only be argued with for so long
headers.label: The Stables
headers.why: kite in the night sky → grey hour, palace stables

headers.before: The star came down past the west wall of the Moon Palace
headers.label: The Scorched Ground
headers.why: after the Hanbyul flashback, back to the present at a new spot (the sacrifice ground)

headers.before: That night, on Radiance’s rampart, Bidam speaks
headers.label: The Rampart
headers.why: Day 9 battle and Alchun → night speech on the rebel wall

headers.before: He rides north with a stone in his sleeve that will not cool.
headers.label: Home to Manno
headers.why: cavern under the ridge → home with Manmyung and the baby, days later

headers.before: They meet again between the camps — not as High Councillor and marshal
headers.label: Between the Camps
headers.why: Bidam saddling Bisamun at his own lines → the duel ground

headers.before: Rain finds the lattice before the physicians do.
headers.label: The Queen’s Bedside
headers.why: muddy field and Kangrim → Sunduk's deathbed indoors, with no cue at all

headers.before: That night Yushin walks out alone to the pavilion between the old camp lines.
headers.label: The Empty Pavilion
headers.why: deathbed → night, the abandoned tea pavilion

headers.before: When he arrived, seeing that Chunchu’s bearing was outstanding, they treated him generously.
headers.label: The Audience Hall
headers.why: ward chief at the lodging → Taizong's hall; the emperor speaks with no setup

headers.before: The Ministry of War can’t find him a general, so Chunchu tries the historians.
headers.label: The History Office
headers.why: palace / ministry → the historian's shelves, new character

headers.before: Chunchu asks one favour no envoy has asked in years.
headers.label: The Imperial Academy
headers.why: envoys' lodging gossip → the Academy lecture halls

headers.before: The days between audiences belong to someone else.
headers.label: The Gyuku Ground
headers.why: emperor's memorial desk → Li Zhi's gyuku field, new character

headers.before: On the morning before he is to leave, a parcel comes to the lodging from the palace.
headers.label: The Lodging
headers.why: banquet hall (night) → lodging the last morning; then the hallway scene is night again

headers.before: Bupmin sails west with the queen’s ode woven into a length of silk.
headers.label: The Woven Ode
headers.why: Secretariat table → Bupmin's embassy to Chang'an, a different year and errand

headers.before: The three kingdoms east of the sea were founded long ago.
headers.label: The Emperor’s Letter
headers.why: Yamato court → an edict from Chang'an to Baekje; reader will assume Kōtoku wrote it

headers.before: In Chang’an the new emperor is still learning how to stand.
headers.label: Sabi
headers.why: Chang'an mourning → Euija and Gyebek in Baekje

headers.before: The news crosses the sea in the eighth month.
headers.label: Surabol
headers.why: Sabi → Chunchu reading the will in Silla, three months on

headers.before: In an anteroom a young concubine waits with the other women
headers.label: Back at Cuiwei
headers.why: Surabol, eighth month → back to the deathbed day in Chang'an; unmarked jump backward in time

headers.before: A year later, on the anniversary, the new emperor comes to the temple
headers.label: Ganye Temple
headers.why: palace anteroom → nunnery, a year later

headers.before: The Harmony Council meets again to enthrone the next king.
headers.label: The Harmony Council
headers.why: Jinduk's deathbed and Kangrim → council chamber

headers.before: He became king. / Of course he did. / Send him horses.
headers.label: Chang’an
headers.why: Chunchu's letter in Surabol → Gaozong reading it across the sea; no cue that we crossed

headers.before: A few years later, Lady Alyoung is born from a Chicken Dragon’s rib
headers.label: Alyeong Well
headers.why: egg field → a second well and a second birth, years later

headers.before: Sixty-one years later, the chronicle says, the king went up into the sky
headers.label: The Five Tombs
headers.why: founding speech → the king's death sixty-one years on

headers.before: Either way, the chest goes on. At Ajinpo an old woman on the shore hauls it in
headers.label: Ajinpo
headers.why: Suro's hall (Gaya version) → Silla beach (Silla version)

headers.before: King Namhae hears about the clever young man in the crescent house
headers.label: Two Kings Later
headers.why: magistrate's verdict → Talhae on the throne decades later

bridges.after: Before the fourth night’s tea, the Moon Palace tries a quieter weapon.
bridges.en: Chunchu is home from the islands. Empty-handed, and early.
bridges.why: Gi left Chunchu across the sea in Yamato and Bidam's whole plan relies on it; here he is suddenly in the Moon Palace handing Bupmin a jar

bridges.after: Your grace is boundless… Your Majesty…!
bridges.en: Then he says a name nobody has been given yet.
bridges.ko: 그러고는 아직 아무도 받지 않은 이름을 부른다.
bridges.why: Muryuk says "Yushin…" in 532, sixty years before Yushin is born; reads as a continuity error

bridges.after: The old Queen would have known it was going to rain.
bridges.en: After the rites, the new queen keeps two men behind.
bridges.ko: 의식이 끝나자 새 여왕은 두 사람을 남긴다.
bridges.why: Jinduk's lines to Yushin and Chunchu float with no room, time or reason to be talking

bridges.after: He asks for one more thing before he goes: Tang court dress
bridges.en: He thanks the emperor at his desk. The talk wanders.
bridges.ko: 감사 인사는 황제의 책상 앞에서 한다. 이야기는 딴 데로 샌다.
bridges.why: Academy → suddenly a private exchange with Taizong ("forgive a barbarian's question") with no place or occasion

bridges.after: One of the two rubbings is for a temple at Jinci
bridges.en: Samhan has its own story about westerners who came east. Chunchu knows it by heart.
bridges.ko: 삼한에도 서쪽에서 온 사람들 이야기가 있다. 춘추는 그걸 외우고 있다.
bridges.why: Gija & Wiman flashback (-108) drops in with no trigger; at minimum it needs a reason to be in Chunchu's head (better: move it, see stories)

bridges.after: My sister sold me that dream for one silk skirt.
bridges.en: The new king’s first council is about Baekje. It is short.
bridges.ko: 새 임금의 첫 회의 안건은 백제다. 회의는 짧다.
bridges.why: Yushin accuses the king of a private grudge with nothing on the page for him to be reacting to

bridges.after: …Did this country start in a kitchen?
bridges.en: At the wedding feast the six chiefs stand up. They have a plan.
bridges.ko: 혼인 잔치에서 여섯 촌장이 일어선다. 그들에겐 계획이 있다.
bridges.why: "We're going to create a brand new country…" is spoken in p blocks by nobody; reader can't tell who is talking or where

stories.logline: Bidam, newly first chair, is the one hand that vetoes Princess Seungman; while Chunchu is abroad the queen collapses, the palace gate shuts on the Council, and Bidam decides—without a vote for the first time—to raise men with Yumjong.
stories.fixes: Jolbon's closing card promises "the council must name who's next", but Gi opens on Chunchu sailing east and spends 18 blocks in Yamato before the Council. Open on the Council veto ("Only one hand stays down" is the hook) and move the Yamato beat to where Bidam hears it from the harbour clerk (block 58), as a short cutaway. Haesang's send-off line ("If you reach the eastern islands…") sits after the Yamato audience; it must come before departure or be cut. The opening line "Chunchu decides to travel to the East, guided by his friend…" is a textbook caption, not a hook. Bidam reusing Chunchu's exact Yamato line to Seungman is a good callback but only lands if the reader saw Yamato first, so keep the Yamato beat short and early in the cutaway. Last beat (Gaya / six eggs) is a good jump-cue.

stories.logline: A sky god falls for a mountain; their eggs become Gaya's kings; Suro, who can't speak when he sees her, marries the foreign princess Heo and lets her sons carry her name.
stories.fixes: Gi set up the question "Gaya — where did it come from?" but the episode never ties back to the word that cuts Yushin. Add one last line before the card that threads the line forward (Heo's blood → Geumgwan → a cart going to Surabol) without naming Muryuk. Two love stories stacked (Ibiga/Jeonggyeon, Suro/Heo) with the same beat (speechless man, commanding woman); trim the first. Chronology inside Heo's arrival tangles: beach → court meeting → hill rite → tent; the trouser offering to the mountain happens on landing, so move it before the court. Block 64 Heo: "It does now." answers a line that is no longer there (dangling). Suro is never the one who wants anything; give him one want (a queen nobody local can sell him).

stories.logline: Days 1–5 of the siege: Bidam and Yushin meet nightly for tea between the camps and argue country versus blood; Chunchu tries the conscience water on Bidam and it finds nothing, and Bidam laughs at the Sacred Bone for thinking it would.
stories.fixes: Strong spine (five pavilion nights, the splash payoff, "Blood is inevitable"). Problems: Chunchu reappears in Surabol with no word that he came back from Yamato (bridge added). The opening block is a quote record; the hook should be Seungman doing the dying queen's hair (block 4), which is already the best beat in the day. Three flashbacks (615, 636, 618) plus the Bupmin cavern detour dilute the tea; consider moving Jade Gate Valley out. Chunchu says "the Secretariat" in 647, four years before it exists (Royal Secretariat is 651). Block 64 has Korean 정자 inside the English.

stories.logline: The youngest prince of a surrendering Gaya trades his crown for one condition: that his descendants live in Silla without shame.
stories.fixes: Too thin to stand alone (20 blocks) and opens in the wrong war: 562 Sadaham taking Daegaya, then jumps back thirty years to Geumgwan without a marker. Open on the cart rolling into Surabol (532) and move the Sadaham beat to Sadaham's own episode. The mystery-box payoff is missing: block 9 promises "before the hall, the field. The tall Gaya cone still fights" but no field is shown. That field is the cone helm watching the Baekje king die in The Severing, the reveal this episode exists for. Show it. Muryuk calling out "Yushin…" decades before Yushin is born needs the bridge (or move it to an old-man beat).

stories.logline: Days 6–9: Yushin breaks courtesy, is called a Gaya wretch, hears his Gaya dead tell him he is enough, edits heaven with a kite, kills his own horse to answer the falling star, and Bidam answers with his "because it is ours" speech.
stories.fixes: Clear emotional arc for Yushin. Days 8 and 9 hop palace → stables → scorched ground → rebel lines → rampart with no sub-headers (added). Blocks 1–2 and Muryuk's closing line all say "Sixth night" and the two cups: cut one. Day 7 opens with Bidam in the cavern without saying how a besieging commander slipped away; one clause would fix it. Ending: Bidam's speech is the climax but the episode is Yushin's; consider closing on Hanseul being named and putting the speech last in Day 9 as-is (it already is) with the card teasing Seohyun. Fine.

stories.logline: A Gaya prince's polite son keeps getting his horse lost outside a Sacred Bone gate; the princess lifts her own bar, escapes her father's locked house through a drain in a storm, and they raise a boy with seven stars on his back.
stories.fixes: Best-structured in this range: clear want (her), obstacle (Sukhuljong, the word Gaya), turn (lightning and the drain), payoff (the name shouted at the gate, the crooked headband). Minor: the last scene label says Daeyang/대량주 while the text says Daeya; pick one. The cavern sequence is long for an origin coda; trim the fox/grandmother tryouts. Cut the Manmyung–Munhee sister aside in block 154 or keep it to one clause.

stories.logline: Day 10: Yushin kills Bidam on the old score (109), orders his house erased with Bidam's own words, sits with the dying queen who asks him to say "Dukman", and goes back alone to the empty pavilion.
stories.fixes: Bidam dies twice. Blocks 9–14 kill him and Kangrim reads his name; blocks 15–24 are the horse and the purge order; then 25–28 Kangrim walks him again and "Bidam falls the way a Hwarang falls". Move 25–27 straight after 14 and cut 28's fall (keep only the kite burning out, which also needs a plant: the "opposite kite" was never set up). Field → deathbed has no cue (header added). Block 55 says "remembers the first day of the rebellion" but the flashback is 612, the first day at the Hwarang hall; fix the wording. Sunduk's deathbed is beautiful and is the true ending; the pavilion and the "You Gaya wretch" echo work as the coda.

stories.logline: The last Sacred Bone is crowned in a padded crown and cannot stop being compared to her cousin.
stories.fixes: No turn and no scene: two near-identical investiture quotes (cut one), a card with a king number in the sub ("신라 제28대 임금"), and floating lines to Yushin and Chunchu with no room (bridge added). Give her one decision: she is the one who chooses to send Chunchu west, which is what the closing card promises anyway. Build the scene at the loom at night with Chunchu: she asks him to go, he says he already packed. Then the closing card earns "Chunchu goes west…!". The goldsmith padding the crown is the right first beat; keep it.

stories.logline: Chunchu goes to Chang'an to borrow an army; he asks the emperor's true name, learns the machine that makes one brush rule a continent, finds that Saluzi is a horse, wins a promise of Baekje and a poem duel, is frightened by Wu, and gets home only because On Gunhae wears his hat.
stories.fixes: The spine is excellent: "What is the correct name for me to call Your Majesty?" pays off in The Last Game with "Li Shimin". But 260 blocks bounce between too many detours: ward register, Ministry rolls, history office plus Qin book-burning flashback, Academy, clan register, Gija & Wiman flashback, two Wu scenes. Cut or move: Gija & Wiman belongs in the Dangun / Old Joseon run, not here. Reorder the end: banquet (night) → hallway with Wu ("a banquet is still going") → last game → parcel morning → Mingde Gate; right now the parcel morning sits between the banquet and the night hallway. Block 3 ("In Chang'an he watches a machine…") comes before he arrives; drop it or move after the audience. Block 6 mentions "the second banner" with no first banner. Block 162 "The Second Emperor reveals he is dying." is a placeholder caption; show it (a cough into the sleeve, a physician at the gallery door). The HALLWAY label is all caps; make it "The Hallway".

stories.logline: Chunchu routes power around the Harmony Council by building a one-seal office that answers only to the throne, then dresses the court in Tang robes but keeps the crowns.
stories.fixes: No opponent on stage: the Council never speaks, so the reform has nothing to beat. Put one uncle in the room (or let the three-month petition be the spine: open on it circling, close on it landing at the Secretariat in one afternoon). Block 12 "Today, the king will reinvent the kingdom" and block 14 "Chunchu establishes…" read as if he is already king; in 651 he is not. Blocks 4 and 13 repeat "a table that has never held a feast". Bupmin's itchy collar (43) should come before he sails (40). The Tang edict at block 50 reads as Yamato's without a header (added). The year shows as undefined in the dump; set the entry year.

stories.logline: The Second Emperor dies; twenty-one-year-old Li Zhi takes the seal and stops the war his father ordered him to stop; Chunchu decides the war is now his; Wu watches a seal change hands, is shaved, and looks up at the new emperor from the nuns' second row.
stories.fixes: Whose story? Li Zhi's grief and Wu's rise compete, and Sabi and Surabol cameo in between. Order is the real problem: Chang'an (5th month) → Sabi → Surabol (8th month) → back to the Chang'an anteroom on the death day, unmarked (header added). Better: keep the whole Chang'an thread together (deathbed → anteroom → Ganye temple) and end on Chunchu reading the Liaodong line ("Then it is mine") as the last scene before the card. Cut the two Sabi blocks or move them to Exile. Two quotes repeat the same will; keep one.

stories.logline: Jinduk dies; the council that Chunchu hollowed out crowns him by the same unanimity; Munhee becomes queen; Yushin fears a grudge; Chunchu writes to Zhi and does not mention Wu.
stories.fixes: The great beat is told, not shown: block 9 summarizes a holdout and the quote at 10 is Alchun declining the throne himself, which the page never explains. Dramatize it: the council offers it to Alchun first, he refuses, and laughs the room into Chunchu. Yushin's "private grudge" line has nothing to react to (bridge added). Sub on the card carries a king number ("신라 제29대 임금"). Block 7 "Queen Jinduk is dead" repeats what Kangrim just showed; cut it. The monologue about Wu's eyes is a strong closing beat; consider ending there rather than on the court summary at 26.

stories.logline: Bupmin, sent to keep a harbour ledger, is corrected by the customs officer's daughter and kisses her under a rain-curtain while her father coughs and pretends not to see.
stories.fixes: Sweet but no obstacle: he wants her, she wants him, the father allows it in one cough. Let the bad sum cost something (a ship mis-tided, a cargo lost) so her correction matters. The second scene (The Next King) skips two reigns in one sentence and calls back "king for all", a line the reader has not heard yet in reading order; either plant it in this episode first or cut the exchange. Opening is fine.

stories.logline: Six chiefs see a white horse kneel at a well; from its egg comes a boy they crown; he marries the dragon-born Alyoung for love, and Silla is founded on a promise that no one will be left outside the gate.
stories.fixes: The horse-and-egg discovery is told four times (blocks 0, 2–3, 5 quote, 6–13, 11 quote). Cut the opening summary and the first quote; start at the ridge with Alpyung asking why a horse is kneeling. Block 0 says "After the fall of Old Joseon", which opens the Old Joseon box before Dangun's episode; drop it. The founding manifesto (18–22) is spoken by nobody (bridge added; better, turn it into chiefs' dialogue). The best beat (the body falling in five pieces, "Nobody records a horse") is a good ending; keep.

stories.logline: A boy who washes up in a chest picks the best house in town, fakes his way into owning it with buried charcoal, and later makes the man he robbed his chief minister.
stories.fixes: Clear con-man tale with a good runner ("Prove it."). The Gaya version with Suro is a fun callback but needs a header to separate it from the Silla beach (added). Block 1 (Dapana backstory) plus its quote tell the same thing; keep one. Last beat links neatly to Alji.

stories.logline: King Talhae, once a boy in a box, finds another boy in a gold box under a crowing rooster and raises him, and the Kim name begins.
stories.fixes: Fine as a short myth coda; Talhae's "Mine was bigger" is the hook. Each event is told twice (narration + quote at 3/4, 5/7, 8/9); cut the paired quotes per the one-quote rule. No one wants anything; give Alji one gesture (he doesn't ask for the throne, on screen). The steam-word plant (block 11) is good. Closing card jumps back to Baekje; fine.
